# lxml parser loading DTDs or without size limits (Python)

`qualor:python/xxe-dtd-options` · Security hotspot · Severity: Medium · [CWE-611](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/611.html), [CWE-776](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/776.html) · OWASP Top 10: [A02:2025 Security Misconfiguration](https://top10.owasp.org/2025/A02_2025-Security_Misconfiguration/), [A05:2021 Security Misconfiguration](https://top10.owasp.org/2021/A05_2021-Security_Misconfiguration/)

> **Security hotspot.** This rule asks for a review: it marks code that is often safe and
> sometimes not, and a person decides which. A hotspot never fails the quality gate.

## What it finds

<!-- begin: what-it-finds -->
lxml XML parsers made with an option that loads the document's DTD or lifts the parser's
security limits, for a person to check what they parse:

- `load_dtd=True`, `dtd_validation=True` or `attribute_defaults=True`, which read the DTD named in
  the document's `DOCTYPE`;
- `huge_tree=True`, which turns off libxml2's limits on tree depth, text size and entity
  expansion.

It covers `etree.XMLParser` (and `ETCompatXMLParser`, `XMLTreeBuilder`), `html.XHTMLParser`,
`etree.XMLPullParser`, `etree.iterparse()` and `objectify.makeparser()`. A parser that [python.xxe](xxe.md) reports (external entities
resolved, or network access with entities or a DTD) is left to it, so that each parser gets one
finding; a parser with network access on, entities off and `huge_tree=True` is reported here.
<!-- end: what-it-finds -->

## Why it matters

<!-- begin: why-it-matters -->
For your own documents, DTD validation and large trees are what these options are for. For
input from users or other systems, the document chooses the DTD: it can make the parser read a
local file as its DTD (CWE-611), and without the limits a small document can expand into a huge
one or nest deeply enough to exhaust memory and CPU (CWE-776, "billion laughs"). The lxml FAQ
advises a parser that loads no external DTD for untrusted content.
<!-- end: why-it-matters -->

## Example

<!-- begin: example -->
**Noncompliant:** an upload is parsed with DTD validation, so the upload picks the DTD.

```python
from lxml import etree


def import_feed(data):
    parser = etree.XMLParser(dtd_validation=True)
    return etree.fromstring(data, parser)
```

**Compliant:** the defaults load no DTD; the feed is validated against a schema the code ships.

```python
from lxml import etree

FEED_SCHEMA = etree.XMLSchema(etree.parse("schemas/feed.xsd"))


def import_feed(data):
    root = etree.fromstring(data)
    FEED_SCHEMA.assertValid(root)
    return root
```
<!-- end: example -->

## How to fix

<!-- begin: how-to-fix -->
- If the parser only sees trusted documents (files you ship or generate), mark the finding as
  reviewed.
- For untrusted input, keep lxml's defaults: no DTD loaded and the security limits on.
- Validate untrusted documents against a schema or DTD the code loads itself
  (`etree.XMLSchema(...)`, `etree.DTD(...)`), not one the document names.
- Use `huge_tree=True` only for large trusted files; for large untrusted input, parse
  incrementally with `iterparse()` and enforce your own size limits.
<!-- end: how-to-fix -->

## Frameworks and APIs covered

- lxml

## Known limits

<!-- begin: known-limits -->
- Options passed as a dict (`XMLParser(**opts)`) are not seen.
- Test code (`test_*.py`, `*_test.py`, `conftest.py`, `tests.py`, `tests/`, `test/`) is not
  scanned.
<!-- end: known-limits -->

The test file [`rules/python/xxe/xxe-dtd-options.py`](../../../rules/python/xxe/xxe-dtd-options.py) holds every case the rule reports or accepts:
lines marked `ruleid:` must be reported and lines marked `ok:` must not. The known limits are
